kf: **Porphyria cutanea tarda (PCT)** is the commonest porphyria: blisters, erosions, **skin fragility**, scars and **milia** on the backs of the hands.
Also facial hypertrichosis and hyperpigmentation; urine may be dark.
Triggers: **alcohol, oestrogens, hepatitis C, HIV, iron overload (haemochromatosis)**, smoking.
Confirm: plasma and urine porphyrins; check ferritin, LFT, hepatitis C, HFE genotype.
Specialist: venesection (iron reduction) or low-dose hydroxychloroquine; remove triggers; visible-light protection.

sub: Adults over 40; about 1 in 10,000–25,000; familial form in about a fifth.

myths: **"Sunscreen protects"**: ordinary sunscreens do not block the visible light (around 400 nm) that excites porphyrins.
patho_lead: Reduced activity of **uroporphyrinogen decarboxylase** in the liver lets **light-sensitive porphyrins** build up in the skin.

mech.t: Iron and oxidative stress (alcohol, hepatitis C, oestrogen) inhibit hepatic UROD.
Uroporphyrins accumulate in the liver, blood and skin.
Visible light (about 400–410 nm) excites porphyrins, generating reactive oxygen that damages the dermo-epidermal junction.
Minor trauma causes subepidermal blisters that heal with scars and milia.
mech.cap: Milia form as blisters heal: tiny keratin cysts just beneath the epidermis.

histo: Cell-poor subepidermal blister with 'festooning' of dermal papillae; caterpillar bodies.

sub: Same skin signs with normal porphyrins: naproxen, tetracyclines, furosemide, sunbeds, dialysis.

comp: Scarring, cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma (in liver disease).
prog: Remits with iron depletion or hydroxychloroquine; relapse if triggers return.
